title: Find and Replace Pattern
statement:
You are given an array of strings `words` and a string `pattern`, all of the same length. A word **fits** the pattern when some one-to-one renaming of letters turns `pattern` into that word: each letter of `pattern` is replaced by one fixed letter everywhere it appears, and two different letters of `pattern` never become the same letter.

Return every word of `words` that fits `pattern`, in any order (a word listed twice in `words` appears twice in the answer). Return an empty list when none fit.
constraints: pattern and every words[i] contain only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

A word fits when its letters line up with the pattern's letters one-to-one. One map is not enough: `pattern = "ab"` and `word = "cc"` give a consistent map `a -> c`, `b -> c`, yet two pattern letters collapse into one. Keeping a second map in the reverse direction catches that. (A slower check compares every pair of positions: equal in the pattern must mean equal in the word, and the other way round.)

## Approach

1. For each `word`, start two empty maps: `toWord` (pattern letter to word letter) and `toPattern` (word letter to pattern letter).
2. Walk position `i`, reading pattern letter `p` and word letter `w`.
3. If neither letter has a partner yet, pair them in both maps.
4. Otherwise both must already be paired with each other; any other combination sets `fits = false` and stops the walk.
5. Add the word to `result` when `fits` survives, and return `result`.

## Example 1, step by step

`pattern = "abb"`. For `"abc"`: `a-a`, `b-b` pair up, then `b` meets `c` but is already paired with `b`, so it fails. `"deq"` fails the same way. For `"mee"`: `a-m`, `b-e`, then `b` meets `e` again, a match, so it fits. `"aqq"` fits likewise. For `"dkd"`, `b` (paired with `k`) meets `d` and fails. For `"ccc"`, `a-c` is paired, then `b` is new but `c` already belongs to `a`, so it fails. The answer is `["mee", "aqq"]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n · L) for `n` words of length `L`: each letter costs O(1) map work.
- Space: O(L) for the two maps of one word, plus the output.

## Pitfalls

- Checking only `toWord` accepts `"ccc"` for `"abb"`; the reverse map is what forbids two letters sharing one image.
- Reset both maps for every word; pairings from one word say nothing about the next.
- Keep duplicate words: each copy that fits is returned.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `result` | the words that fit, in input order |
| `word` | the word being tested |
| `toWord` | pattern letter to the word letter it became |
| `toPattern` | word letter to the pattern letter it came from |
| `fits` | whether the word still matches so far |
| `i`, `p`, `w` | position, pattern letter and word letter there |
